newsitem.title: USA: Qwest Communications files IPO with SEC.
newsitem.headline: Qwest Communications files IPO with SEC.

text.p: Qwest Communications International Inc filed Friday with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission an intial public offering with a proposed maximum value of about $287.5 million.

The Denver-based communications company said Salomon Brothers Inc, Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp, Goldman Sachs & Co, and Merrill Lynch & Co. will underwrite the offering and will have an over-allotment option.

The company did not disclose the exact amount of the public offering or the estimated share price in the preliminary filing. However, a portion of the shares to be offered, are expected to be sold outside the United States and Canada.

Proceeds from the sale will be used primarily to fund capital expenditures required to back the company's network and to purchase fiber cable and other materials including electronic equipment. The company said it will also use the proceeds to repay about $28 million in oustanding advances.
In 1996, the company reported a net loss of $6.9 million on total revenue of $230.996 million. That compares to a 1995 net loss of $25.1 million on revenue of $125 million.
